description: Telemetry Dynamics ekibi olarak gerçek zamanlı veri mimarileri ve uzay sistemlerine ilgi duyuyoruz. Amacımız teoride kalmayan, işlevsel yazılımlar geliştirmek; bu kapsamda astronot telemetri sistemleri üzerinde çalışıyoruz. Bize katılarak yazılım ve sistem geliştirme becerilerinizi gerçek bir üründe uygulayabilir, disiplinli bir ekiple sıfırdan üretim yapabilirsiniz. Ekibimizde modern frontend geliştirme ve veri akışı süreçlerinde rol alabilecek, sorumluluk sahibi takım arkadaşları arıyoruz.
summary: OrbitalPulse represents an innovative periodic and context-sensitive telemetry framework that has been designed for assessing the health metrics of astronauts in the micro-gravity conditions of ISS, overcoming the limitations and discomfort associated with the constant 24/7 usage of wearable or wire-based biosensors. This framework makes use of natural points of interactions of astronauts in their day-to-day activities, such as using exercise machines (ARED, treadmills), using mission consoles, and common places, to collect smart data as nodes. While the astronauts interact with these points, immediate health metrics are gathered with the help of non-invasive PPG and authentication techniques. Through time-series analysis of these periodic metrics, the system provides a continuous health profile of the astronaut without putting any physical or psychological pressure on him/her.

PROJECT DETAILS: ORBITAL-PULSE

Enterprise ISS Crew Health Monitoring, Cumulative Physiological Risk Assessment, and Environment-Based Telemetry Architecture

1. Executive Summary & Problem Statement

Long-duration spaceflight missions aboard the International Station (ISS) and upcoming deep-space architectures expose astronauts to severe physiological and psychological stressors. These include galactic cosmic radiation (GCR), solar particle events (SPE), microgravity-induced bone mineral density (BMD) loss, skeletal muscle atrophy, fluid redistribution, autonomic cardiovascular deconditioning, and behavioral health challenges arising from long-term isolation and confinement.

Traditional medical telemetry relies heavily on continuous, 24/7 wired or wireless wearable sensors. However, in the high-mobility, operational environment of the ISS, continuous wearables create significant operational friction, data noise, battery management overhead, and physical discomfort for the crew. Furthermore, astronauts on long missions carry a critical responsibility for self-monitoring and recognizing early sub-clinical degradation vectors in themselves before they manifest into acute medical events.

OrbitalPulse solves this challenge by deploying a robust, sensorless, Environment-Based Periodic Telemetry and Crew Self-Evaluation Architecture. Instead of forcing intrusive continuous monitoring, OrbitalPulse integrates data capture points naturally into the daily station routine—such as physical interactions with the Advanced Resistive Exercise Device (ARED) in Node 3, sleep station logs, and periodic subjective questionnaires. Combined with live real-time internet data feeds (NOAA Space Weather and ISS orbital telemetry), OrbitalPulse provides a comprehensive, closed-loop health monitoring and automated countermeasure ecosystem.

2. System Architecture & Core Logic

OrbitalPulse is engineered as an enterprise-grade Python application utilizing Streamlit, Plotly, Pandas, NumPy, and live REST APIs. The system architecture is divided into three primary layers:

  1. Live External OSINT & Orbital Ingestion Layer:

    • Fetches real-time ISS orbital coordinates (Latitude, Longitude, Altitude, Velocity) via the Where The ISS At API.
    • Ingests real-time space weather data from the NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) REST endpoints to track geomagnetic Kp-indices and radiation flux in real-time.
    • Simulates time-series degradation matrices for active ISS crew rosters (including Expedition 72/73 commanders and SpaceX Crew-9 flight engineers such as Sunita Williams, Butch Wilmore, Nick Hague, and Aleksandr Gorbunov).
    • Calculates multi-system risk vectors including Bone Mineral Density (BMD) decay curves against safety floors, skeletal muscle retention percentages, and autonomic cardiovascular strain indices.
    • Empowers astronauts to log subjective metrics (sleep duration, fatigue levels, vestibular adaptation, muscle soreness) securely.
    • Automatically cross-references inputs against environmental radiation and mission duration data to output actionable, autonomous medical and exercise countermeasures.

3. Detailed Breakdown of System Modules

Module 01: Live Orbital Telemetry & OSINT Command

  • Functionality: Serves as the primary operational dashboard for ground control and crew members.
  • Live Ingestion: Displays real-time ISS coordinates fetched directly from internet APIs alongside mission duration counters and active safety floor thresholds.
  • Alert Matrix: Triggers automated warnings if geomagnetic storm activity (NOAA Kp-index) or isolation stress metrics cross pre-determined operational safety margins.

Module 02: Cumulative Physiological Risk (BMD & Skeletal Muscle Loss)

  • Functionality: Monitors long-duration microgravity adaptation.
  • Bone Resorption Tracking: Visualizes 12-week time-series degradation curves of Bone Mineral Density (BMD) against dynamic safety floors, highlighting osteoclast activity and urinary calcium excretion trends.
  • Muscle Atrophy Analysis: Evaluates skeletal muscle mass retention and correlates it with ARED (Advanced Resistive Exercise Device) resistance protocol logs.

Module 03: Radiation & Environmental Exposure Tracker

  • Functionality: Tracks cumulative ionizing radiation dosages (measured in mSv) against 12-month career safety limits (1,000 mSv ceiling).
  • Space Weather Correlation: Integrates live planetary Kp-indices and solar flux data to assess orbital shielding efficacy and potential solar particle event (SPE) risks.

Module 04: Crew Self-Assessment & Metabolic Logs

  • Functionality: Provides an autonomous daily reporting interface.
  • Subjective Metrics: Captures sleep debt, perceived physical fatigue, and vestibular/spatial orientation status (tracking fluid shifts and space motion adaptation).
  • Nutritional Tracking: Monitors caloric balance (thermostabilized rations), hydration compliance (2,800 mL/day targets), and targeted micronutrient/vitamin D3 supplementation.

Module 05: Mission Control Diagnostics & Automated Alert Engine

  • Functionality: Acts as the automated decision-support system.
  • Terminal Simulation: Features a secure terminal interface displaying encrypted AES-256-GCM data packet verifications, CRC-32 checksums, and wireless local bus synchronization logs across ISS nodes (Node 1 Zvezda, Node 2 Harmony, Node 3 Quarters/Gym, Destiny Lab).
  • Countermeasure Generation: Automatically generates specific recommendations (e.g., adjusting ARED deadlift load by 5%, scheduling private psychological downlinks, or altering circadian lighting schedules).

Module 06: Massive OSINT Data Stream & Raw CSV Telemetry Export

  • Functionality: Big-data simulation and engineering archival.
  • High-Frequency Generation: Instantly synthesizes 50,000+ high-frequency telemetry rows containing timestamped orbital, BMD, muscle, and radiation samples on the fly.
  • Data Export: Enables offline engineering analysis by allowing operators to download comprehensive CSV telemetry packages for any active crew member.

4. Technology Stack & Deployment

  • Language: Python 3.14+
  • Frontend & Dashboard: Streamlit (Custom Aerospace Mission Control CSS Theme)
  • Data Visualization: Plotly (Interactive multi-vector time-series, polar risk radars, and degradation curves)
  • Data Processing: Pandas, NumPy
  • Live Networking: Requests library for real-time REST API integration with NOAA SWPC and satellite tracking endpoints.
  • Version Control & Hosting: GitHub Public Repository with direct cloud deployment configuration.

5. Mission Impact & Future Scalability

OrbitalPulse transitions astronaut healthcare from reactive treatment to proactive, environment-aware mitigation. By eliminating the need for intrusive hardware while harnessing live environmental and self-evaluation data, OrbitalPulse provides a scalable, resilient health monitoring blueprint not only for the International Space Station, but for future deep-space transit vehicles, lunar Gateway outposts, and long-duration Martian exploration missions.
